newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dlr/mark to struggle past recent 2-yr peak.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dlr/mark to struggle past recent 2-yr peak.

text.p: The dollar plowed through key resistance at the December 1996 high of 1.5735 marks to hit a fresh two-year peak at 1.5787, and strategists said the greenback is positioned to extend the move higher.
But it will be tough going as dealers cited many layers of closely packed resistance ahead of the rally's ultimate target of 1.6060 marks, a three-year, 62-percent retracement.

"I think we're going to run into some tough resistance between 1.5770/75 marks, which we already have challenged somewhat, and 1.5875 marks," said Thom Worden, global technical analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Worden cited a number of channel tops which come in at 1.5870/75 marks.
The main hurdle for the dollar is the 1.5820/30 mark level, which reflects a series of highs seen in December 1994.
"The highs from two years ago are technically more important than the 1.58 figure. I think we will see a break of those highs in the near-term," said Ben Morden, technical analyst at I.D.E.A.
Morden has a two-week dollar/mark objective of 1.59, but he expressed concern that given Wednesday's rapid rise, his target date might be too far out.
Technicians said the recent gain in the U.S. unit against the yen lacks the momentum of the dollar/mark run-up and they were divided on whether it would penetrate resistance at 116.00/20 yen.
"I don't expect it to climb over 116.20 in this up move and I think the risk in the short-term is down," Worden said .
While Morden agreed dollar/yen lacked the strength of dollar/mark, he forecast a surge through Monday's 45-month high of 116.98 yen by Friday.
He added that trendline resistance dating from September 1995 comes in at 117 yen.
Also, dollar/yen support at 115, which has proved a solid floor in the recent past, may easily crumble when next tested, analysts said.
"The 115 level has been good support in the past, but I'm not sure it will be good support anymore. I think if we see that level again, we will see dollar/yen go lower to 114 to 113.80," Worden said.
